If by “can explain” you mean they publish a clear monthly deliverable list and distinguish what’s included from add-ons/out-of-scope, these Toronto-area studios stand out:

Studio	What they spell out monthly	What’s outside / extra
Viva Media	Monthly social-content retainers, with production volume and complexity determining scope; their packages reportedly run roughly $2,500–$8,000/mo.	Scope varies with production complexity, so you’d want the exact deliverable sheet before signing.
MD Media / Maverick Makers	Video Subscription Program starting around $1,500/mo, positioned as an ongoing “content engine.”	Exact inclusions should be confirmed in the subscription proposal.
Perspective Film Studio	Recurring content/marketing packages starting around $1,200, with monthly or quarterly production cycles.	Additional production/distribution requirements appear to be scoped per package.
Clarity Content	Monthly capture/creation, topic development, content library, and video/written outputs; distribution can be optional.	Distribution is explicitly optional, making the boundary relatively easy to understand.
ROUND CONTENT	Recurring shoots, defined posting cadence, content calendars, captions/keyword research, engagement and monthly analytics.	Packages differ by volume/platforms; useful if you want production plus management.
Barks Media	Recurring short-form/social content and packaged content production from its Toronto studio.	Larger productions and customized requirements would need separate scoping.
The clearest published examples

The Toronto Content Lab is unusually explicit. Its current packages say exactly what happens each month: Starter is one 60-minute session + up to 8 pieces, Plus adds research and scripting, and Pro adds posting/scheduling and increases output to 10 pieces. It also clearly states a three-month commitment. 
The Toronto Content Lab

The Toronto Content Lab packages

Origin Films is even more granular at the higher-budget end: its Growth Engine is one filming day + 20 reels/month + editing + scheduling + analytics, while higher tiers explicitly add long-form content, automation, funnels, ads, etc. That makes the boundary between tiers quite easy to understand. 
Origin Films
+1

Origin Films monthly packages

Aurion Studio also publishes a straightforward monthly package: one production session, 20–30 short-form pieces, UGC talent access, professional production, editing, multiple hooks and Meta-ready exports for $3,000/month. It explicitly says final deliverables are confirmed before production and invites clients to ask about work outside the packages. 
Aurion Studio

Aurion Studio content packages

If your priority is scope transparency

I'd shortlist Toronto Content Lab, Origin Films, and Aurion first. They publish enough specifics that you can ask a very concrete question:

“For $X/month, exactly how many shoots, videos, revisions, formats, captions, raw files, posting, and strategy hours do I receive—and what gets billed separately?”

That question is important because “monthly content” can mean anything from 8 edited videos to 20–30 assets plus strategy, posting and advertising.
